title: Enable kernel selector v2 canary in us-east (5% cohort)
author: Connor O'Brien
description:
Context: This PR is the first staged enablement of kernel selector v2 in Hosted for runtime-1.19. It flips the rollout config to enable selector v2 for a small 5% canary cohort in us-east only, leaving all other regions at 0% and preserving deterministic fallback to selector v1. This is intentionally config-only (no code changes) to keep rollback fast.

What changes:
- Enables selector_v2 in us-east at 5% for Hosted traffic only (Dedicated/Private remain disabled by default).
- Uses stable hashing on (org_id, model_family) to avoid churn across deploys and keep perf attribution consistent.
- Adds explicit allowlist constraints: only Llama-family + Mistral-family at first; unknown model families continue to force v1/safe kernel set.
- Leaves kill switch in place (runtime.kernel_selector.v2.force_disable=true) with highest precedence.

Monitoring / rollout checklist:
- Follow: https://drive.google.com/.../kernel-selector-v2-rollout-checklist (section: "Stage 1: 5% us-east")
- Guardrails / rollback criteria: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/.../selector-v2-rollout-slo-guardrails
- Dashboards to watch (minimum): Runtime Perf Overview (p95 latency by gpu_sku), Selector v2 Breakdown (selector_version/kernel_id heatmap), Correctness (NaN rate, shape mismatch errors), and Request error rate.

Config details:
- Flag: runtime.kernel_selector.selector_version = "v2" (for cohort)
- Cohort: hosted/us-east/percent = 5
- Constraints: model_family in {llama, mistral}; gpu_sku in {L4, A10, A100, H100} (all supported, but watch A10 long-context specifically)

Rollback plan:
- Immediate: set hosted/us-east/percent = 0 (safe, no restart needed; config reload)
- Emergency: set runtime.kernel_selector.v2.force_disable = true (global)
- Validate rollback: selector_version metric returns to v1 baseline within 10 minutes; p95/p99 revert to pre-canary bands; NaN/shape mismatch alerts clear.

Files / areas touched:
- runtime/config/rollouts/kernel_selector_v2.yaml
- runtime/config/regions/us-east.yaml
- runtime/config/README_rollout_process.md (added note on cohort hashing + precedence)
- ops/runbooks/runtime_release_1_19.md (links to dashboards + rollback switch)

Illustrative snippet (final):
- hosted:
  - region: us-east
    kernel_selector_v2:
      enabled_percent: 5
      model_family_allowlist: ["llama", "mistral"]
      cohort_key: "org_id:model_family"
      selector_version: "v2"

Notes:
- This stage is blocked on green canary checks from ENG-3930; release eng will keep the cohort at 5% for >=24h unless SLOs/guardrails trigger rollback.
- If we see A10 long-context regressions, do not expand cohort; instead pin A10 long-context to v1 via per-gpu override in the same file (see comments in config).

Review conversation (highlights):
- Aisha Bello (SRE): "Please call out exact rollback thresholds and confirm kill-switch precedence. Also: ensure we don’t accidentally include Dedicated." Connor: "Updated description + added config comment for precedence; Dedicated explicitly set to 0% in the same file." 
- Allison Grant (Obs standards): "Are we bucketing labels for kernel_choice? This rollout will increase cardinality." Connor: "No new labels added in this PR; telemetry bucketing is already in runtime-1.19 via pr_18519. This is just enablement." 
- Grace Kim (Kernel selection): "Can we start with llama/mistral only? Qwen is still being tuned." Connor: "Yes—added model_family allowlist; Qwen remains v1 until pr_18533 is fully baked + benchmarked." 
- Benji Okafor (Flags/config): "Make sure cohort hashing is stable across config reloads." Connor: "We use org_id+model_family stable key (documented in README); no randomness." 

CI:
- ✅ config-validate
- ✅ unit (runtime-config)
- ✅ lint
- ✅ policy-check (no prod-wide enablement)

Merge:
- Squash merged into release/runtime-1.19. Release train will pick this up for the us-east canary window on 2026-02-12 18:00 PT.
